scope.no_live_claim: Source and metadata only; no build/process/game/Wine/display/harness/live-lock action.

side_definitions.server: logical server VM/app/object seam: CServerExoAppInternal, CVirtualMachineInternal/CVirtualMachine, CSWS* EventHandler.
side_definitions.client: client/input DoConsole seam; client MainLoop does not dispatch events.
side_definitions.processlocal: host lifecycle outside engine event seams.
side_definitions.unimplemented: public constant with no C++ dispatch site; name alone gives no side.
side_definitions.unresolved: source dispatch exists but build address binding is unresolved.

architecture.answer: Server-event bound with client-local console and process-local lifecycle; embedded processes contain logical client and server objects but Lua event dispatch is not symmetric. Split Role::Client/Role::Server changes transport behavior, not client-side event dispatch.
architecture.client_main_loop: app.client_main_loop is optional harness/overlay post-frame work and calls no Host::dispatch.
architecture.logical_vs_process: Executable role, logical engine object, and caller thread are distinct. A split client may have a support-server object while authority is remote; this is not client-side Lua proof.
architecture.threading: server MainLoop latches engine owner before console/harness/Lua; startup worker raises lifecycle before VM capture.
architecture.transport: socket thread moves opaque frames; engine work is drained on owner thread.

contract.doc: Called once after the script loads. `build` is the identified game build, e.g. k1_steam_103.
Called before the script is unloaded, including on reload and on quarantine.

Called for every line typed into the cheat console, including lines the
game does not recognise. Return false to consume the line so the game never sees it,
which is how a script adds its own commands. The console hook receives one keystroke
at a time and buffers to a line, so this fires on Enter.

Called after an NWScript finishes. `ran` is the engine's own return value:
true when the script loaded and ran with a balanced stack.

Return a string to persist alongside the save. It comes back to OnLoad when
that save is loaded.
Receives whatever OnSave returned when this save was written.

Called once per server frame. The highest-frequency callback: a script
that does not define it pays nothing, one that does should keep the body short.
Return false to stop the game's own script running.
